title: Gukesh opens world title defence against Sindarov in Geneva tonight, with Black
dek: The 20-year-old Indian champion faces Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov, 72 rating points above him, over 14 games for a $2.5 million prize fund. Game 1 starts at 7.30 pm IST.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
D. Gukesh begins the defence of his world chess title on Tuesday against Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan, in a 14-game match at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, on the edge of Geneva. Game 1 starts at 3 pm local time, 7.30 pm IST, and Gukesh will have the black pieces after the colours were drawn at the opening ceremony.

Both players are 20; Sindarov turns 21 on 8 December. Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world champion in December 2024 when he beat China's Ding Liren 7.5-6.5 in Singapore. Sindarov earned his challenge by winning the 2026 Candidates Tournament in Cyprus with 10 points from 14 games, six wins and no losses, finishing 1.5 points clear of Anish Giri with a round to spare. "I'm here to win it all over again," Gukesh said before the match, according to reports.

## The match

The first player to 7.5 points wins. The schedule runs in blocks of three games followed by a rest day, with rest days on 27 November and 1, 5 and 9 December. Game 14 is on 11 December, and tiebreaks, if needed, on 12 December. Sindarov has White in the odd-numbered games and Gukesh in the even-numbered ones.

Each side gets 120 minutes for the first 40 moves and then 30 more minutes for the rest of the game, with 30 seconds added for each move from move 41. To discourage quick draws, the players cannot agree a draw before Black's 40th move; before that a game can only be drawn by threefold repetition or stalemate, claimed through the arbiter.

If the score is 7-7, the match goes to four rapid games of 15 minutes plus 10 seconds a move, then two games of 10 minutes plus 5 seconds, then two blitz games of 3 minutes plus 2 seconds, and finally single blitz games with colours reversed until someone wins.

The prize fund is $2.5 million, net of local taxes. Each player earns $200,000 for every game he wins, with the rest divided under set rules; if the match goes to tiebreaks, the winner receives $1.3 million and the loser $1.2 million.

## Form and history

On paper Gukesh starts as the underdog. On November's rating list Sindarov is world number four at 2782, while Gukesh is 2710 and 26th, a gap of 72 points; he dropped below 2700 on the live list during this year's Olympiad, according to reports. Sindarov also leads their classical head-to-head 2-0 with one draw, from wins at the 2018 Moscow Open and the 2022 Sharjah Masters and a draw at Tata Steel in January. Gukesh did beat him in a rapid game at a tournament in May.

Gukesh's own path to the title in 2024 began as an outsider too: he won the Candidates in Toronto at 17 before beating Ding in a match that went to the final game.

## What to watch

The match is the first world championship between two players born in the 21st century. Peter Svidler and Peter Leko are the official commentators on FIDE's broadcast. The first rest day follows Game 3 on Thursday.
